questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Drift across SAP components in multi-region AWS deployments is common. This tests practical governance: real-time drift detection, automated remediation, and IaC for cross-region controls.

## Key Concepts

- AWS Config custom rules for multi-region drift
- Cross-account IAM roles and SCPs
- SSM Automation and Step Functions orchestration
- PrivateLink endpoints and SAP components

## Code Example

```yaml
Resources:
  SAPDriftRule:
    Type: AWS::Config::ConfigRule
    Properties:
      ConfigRuleName: SAPDriftRule
      Source:
        Owner: CUSTOM_LAMBDA
        SourceIdentifier: SAPDriftLambda
      InputParameters: {}
      Scope:
        ComplianceResourceTypes:
          - AWS::EC2::Instance
          - AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
  SAPRemediationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Path: /
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPRemediation
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: 2012-10-17
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: ["ssm:SendCommand","ssm:ListCommands","ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation"]
                Resource: "*"
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test drift remediation safety when a rule fires?
- How would you scale the remediation across regions and accounts?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical, low-risk patch management for SAP on AWS with governance and rollback.

## Key Concepts

- AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
- Patch Baselines and Maintenance Windows
- IAM roles for SSM
- CloudFormation automation

## Code Example

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  SAPPatchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Path: '/'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPPatchAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:SendCommand
                  - ssm:ListCommands
                  - ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation
                Resource: '*'
  SAPOSPatchBaseline:
    Type: AWS::SSM::PatchBaseline
    Properties:
      Name: SAP-OS-PatchBaseline
      OperatingSystem: 'AMAZON_LINUX_2'
      ApprovalRules:
        PatchRules:
          - PatchFilterGroup:
              PatchFilters:
                - Key: 'CLASSIFICATION'
                  Values:
                    - 'Security'
                    - 'Critical'
            ComplianceLevel: 'CRITICAL'
            ApproveAfterDays: 0
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend this to multi-region deployments?
- How would you enforce change-control and auditing for patch events?
- How would you validate SAP service health after patches without impacting users?

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses practical knowledge of enterprise patch governance across multiple AWS accounts for SAP workloads running on EC2. It tests understanding of AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager, cross-account access patterns, and automated compliance monitoring.

## Key Concepts
- AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager for automated patching
- Cross-account IAM roles with trust policies
- Patch baselines and approval rules
- Maintenance windows for scheduled patching
- CloudWatch alarms for compliance monitoring
- AWS Config and SSM compliance reports for auditing

## Minimal IaC Snippet (CloudFormation)

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Cross-account patch management resources

Resources:
  CrossAccountRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: ssm-patch-manager-role
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: arn:aws:iam::SHARED_ACCOUNT_ID:root
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore

  SAPPatchBaseline:
    Type: AWS::SSM::PatchBaseline
    Properties:
      Name: sap-weekly-patch-baseline
      OperatingSystem: AMAZON_LINUX_2
      ApprovalRules:
        Rules:
          - PatchFilterGroup:
              PatchFilters:
                - Key: MSRC_SEVERITY
                  Values: [Critical, Important]
                - Key: CLASSIFICATION
                  Values: [SecurityUpdates, BugfixUpdates]
            PatchSet: AWS_DEFAULT
            ApproveAfterDays: 7
      Description: Weekly SAP OS patch baseline for critical and important updates
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of fundamental AWS networking for SAP: private isolation, controlled admin access, and audit-friendly egress.

## Key Concepts
- VPC design with private subnets for SAP components
- Bastion host as controlled admin access point
- NAT gateway for outbound updates
- Security groups enforcing least privilege on SAP ports
- Basic cost- and log-awareness with flow logs

## Code Example
```terraform
# Minimal Terraform example for core resources
provider "aws" { region = "us-east-1" }

# VPC
resource "aws_vpc" "sap_vpc" {
  cidr_block = "10.0.0.0/16"
  enable_dns_support = true
  enable_dns_hostnames = true
}

# Subnets
resource "aws_subnet" "private_a" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.0.1.0/24"
  availability_zone = "us-east-1a"
}
resource "aws_subnet" "private_b" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.0.2.0/24"
  availability_zone = "us-east-1b"
}
resource "aws_subnet" "public_bastion" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.0.3.0/24"
  availability_zone = "us-east-1a"
  map_public_ip_on_launch = true
}

# Internet & NAT
resource "aws_internet_gateway" "igw" { vpc_id = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id }
resource "aws_nat_gateway" "nat" {
  allocation_id = aws_eip.nat.id
  subnet_id     = aws_subnet.public_bastion.id
}
resource "aws_eip" "nat" { vpc = true }

# Security Groups
resource "aws_security_group" "sap_sg" {
  name        = "sap_sg"
  description = "SAP ports restricted"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
}
resource "aws_security_group" "bastion_sg" {
  name        = "bastion_sg"
  description = "Bastion host access"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
}

# Ingress rules
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "sap_ingress" {
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 30015
  to_port           = 30019
  protocol          = "tcp"
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.sap_sg.id
  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion_sg.id
}
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "sap_ingress2" {
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 3200
  to_port           = 3205
  protocol          = "tcp"
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.sap_sg.id
  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion_sg.id
}
# SSH access to Bastion only from corporate IPs
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "bastion_ssh" {
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 22
  to_port           = 22
  protocol          = "tcp"
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion_sg.id
  cidr_blocks       = ["203.0.113.0/24"]
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design cross-account backup and residency controls in AWS SAP, with auditable trails and proper security controls.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-account IAM roles and Service Control Policies (SCPs)
- AWS S3 backups with data residency requirements
- KMS encryption and S3 bucket policies
- CloudTrail and AWS Config for auditing
- Infrastructure as Code (CloudFormation/CDK)

## Architecture Overview

The solution uses two AWS accounts (Prod and Compliance) with:
- Regional data residency enforcement via SCPs restricting resource creation
- Cross-account IAM role in the Compliance account for Prod to write backups
- S3 bucket policy enforcing bucket location and access controls
- CloudTrail logging all API calls for audit trails

## Code Example

```yaml
Resources:
  SAPBackupRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: arn:aws:iam::PROD_ACCOUNT_ID:root
      Path: /
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPBackupPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Action:
                  - s3:PutObject
                  - s3:ListBucket
                Effect: Allow
                Resource:
                  - arn:aws:s3:::eu-backups-bucket
                  - arn:aws:s3:::eu-backups-bucket/*

  BackupBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: eu-backups-bucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DenyOutsideEU
            Effect: Deny
            Action: s3:*
            NotPrincipal:
              AWS: arn:aws:iam::COMPLIANCE_ACCOUNT_ID:root
            Resource:
              - arn:aws:s3:::eu-backups-bucket
              - arn:aws:s3:::eu-backups-bucket/*
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                s3:Region: eu-west-1
```
